int_name: N HOWARD ST & W TIOGA ST

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features sidewalks on both sides of the street and a basic, though faded, marked crosswalk. Safety is compromised by a lack of traffic control at the intersection and visual obstructions created by parked vehicles near the crossing point.

hazards.name: Faded crosswalk markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings are significantly worn, making the crossing less visible to approaching motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, across the side street

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street near the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of traffic control
hazards.description: There are no visible stop signs or signals to regulate vehicle flow at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Replace faded parallel lines with continental-style high-visibility markings to increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and further prevent illegal parking near the corner.

result.summary: This residential street environment lacks basic pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, curb ramps, and traffic control devices. While sidewalks are present on both sides, they are narrow and the intersection is compromised by parked vehicles that obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks or signage to indicate a pedestrian crossing point at the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles are located very close to the intersection corners, blocking the view between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right and left sides of the street near the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends in a vertical curb without a ramp, creating a barrier for people with mobility devices or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install zebra-striped crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: ADA-Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install sloped curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces at all crossing points.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a marked continental crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While the intersection is stop-controlled, parked vehicles near the crossing points create significant visual obstructions that may hinder sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked immediately adjacent to the crosswalk obscure the view of pedestrians waiting to cross, particularly children or those using mobility aids.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbs on both sides of the street leading up to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Warning Signage
hazards.description: There are no pedestrian crossing signs to alert drivers to the presence of the crosswalk beyond the pavement markings.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection approach.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20-30 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to act as a speed table and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides but lacks any marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices. The roadway pavement is in poor condition with visible cracking and patching, and parked vehicles along the curb create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Significant cracking and uneven surfaces in the roadway can cause tripping hazards or affect vehicle handling.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground and mid-ground of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected without right-of-way clarity.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible street segment

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility around parked cars.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the degraded pavement to ensure a smooth and predictable surface for all road users.
